newsitem.title: USA: Texas Instruments to sell holdings - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Texas Instruments to sell holdings - WSJ.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc is planning to sell its defense electronics holdings worth more than $2 billion and McDonnell Douglas Corp is one of the interested buyers, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper cited "people familiar with initial bids offered this week" as saying the sale could take weeks or months to close.
It said the holdings included the manufacture of missile sensors and seekers, advanced aircraft radars, and night vision systems. The holdings generated $1.74 billion in revenue last year, it added.
The newspaper said other bidders included Raytheon Co, Northrop Grumman Corp and Hughes Electronics Corp of General Motors Corp.
It said Lockheed Martin was not interested in the sale because it had already spent $9.1 billion for much of Loral Corp earlier this year.
The newspaper said the terms of the sale set out by Texas Instruments would structure the sale as a "Morris Trust" transaction so as to give it a way to get rid of assets without paying taxes.
